resources.string: PHONE AUDIO\nvideos & music playing on this phone
Listening with: phone audio (what the phone plays)
Phone audio keeps working when you switch to a video app; Android will ask to allow screen/audio capture. The microphone cannot hear the bass of the phone\'s own speaker.

Coyote not found or won\'t connect? Close the DG-Lab app, then power-cycle the box: turn it OFF, turn it ON, and turn the A and B wheels in opposite directions until the wolf eye blinks 5 times — that is pairing mode. Then SCAN.
Opossum not found? Press its power button 5 times until the Bluetooth icon turns yellow, then SCAN.

WRONG BEAT? SHIFT DOWNBEAT BY ONE
Microphone permission is required. Grant it in Settings and reopen.
Phone audio capture was not allowed — still using the microphone.
Waveform restarts on each beat (off = continuous loop, like the official app)

Each device has its own sensitivity. Left = strict: fires only on a confidently locked, steady beat (use for the Coyote). Right = eager: fires sooner and on looser beats (fine for the Opossum). In the header, ♪ counts detected kicks, lock %% is how periodic they are, and the C: / O: line shows each device\'s trigger tempo range and whether it fires now (▶ firing, ✗bpm outside its range, ✗lock beat not solid enough for it, · no beat).
Mini window when leaving the app
Fall back to microphone if phone audio stops
Every window, at the tempo peak
Also detect screen movement (only while the mini window is showing)

How solid the beat must be before this device fires. Strict: only a clearly locked, steady beat (safer for e-stim, may miss loose tracks). Eager: fires on looser or softer beats (fine for vibration, more false triggers in noisy rooms).

How much of each pulse\'s waveform is delivered. 100 %% is the waveform as designed; lower it to soften every pulse without touching the strength limits. Use when the max feels right but each hit is too sharp.

Pulse frequency for the simple pulse (ignored when a library waveform is selected). Low values feel like a slow throb or thump, high values like a fast buzz or tingle. Try 20–40 for a drum-like hit, 100+ for a buzz.
Hard ceiling. Written into the Coyote itself, so nothing in this app can exceed it. Set it while stationary at a level you can definitely take, then leave it.
Base strength (slow tempo) and the floor of the random level. Raise it if quiet or slow songs feel like nothing.
On: faster music = stronger, from the slow-tempo value up to MAX between the two BPM points in Timing. Off: always the slow-tempo value.
Every 0.5–3 s a new level is drawn between base and MAX, mostly low, sometimes near MAX. Overrides tempo mapping. Good when the tempo never changes and you want surprise.
Bluetooth and the box add delay, so pulses are sent early. If pulses feel late, move left (earlier); if they land before the beat, move right. Tune once with a steady track.
How long one pulse lasts. Short = a tap on the beat; long = a hold that can run into the next beat. Library waveforms restart from their beginning on each pulse and play for this long.
Pattern of each pulse, from the official DG-Lab library. The simple pulse is one flat tone; library patterns have their own rhythm and texture.
On the beat: the pattern restarts on every beat and lasts the pulse length. Continuous: the pattern loops like in the official app; only the strength follows the music.
Once per bar = only the first beat of every 4 (needs the bar to be found). Every beat, or 2× / 4× per beat for double- and quadruple-time.
This device only fires when the locked tempo is inside the range. Use it to keep the Coyote quiet on slow songs, or the Opossum only on fast ones. Both ends at the extremes = any tempo.

Instead of every beat: Peak mode owes one pulse per window and releases it at the tempo\'s high point (up to 3 owed; 3 = fired at MAX). Random mode fires at unpredictable intervals within your range. Timer modes are the only trigger while on.
How long each vibration lasts. Motors need ~150 ms to spin up, so very short values are barely felt; 250–400 ms is a clear buzz per beat.
On: every detected kick vibrates immediately, no beat lock needed, so it reacts within a moment of music starting. Off: waits for a locked tempo and uses the sensitivity / rate / range below.

Reads the shared screen at 80×80 and treats frame-to-frame change as movement. Dance hits and cuts fire the chosen devices even when the BPM reading lags a fast dance. This app\'s own window is ignored.
If the screen capture is stopped by the system, switch to the microphone. Off = stop listening instead, so room noise never fires the devices unless you tap MICROPHONE yourself.
The two tempos between which strength scales: at the slow BPM you get the base / min value, at the fast BPM the max. Set them to the tempo range of the music you play.
Also drive the second output (Coyote: channel B electrodes; Opossum: motor B) with the same pattern and level.
On: vibration strength scales between min and max with tempo. Off: a fixed strength.
When you leave the app, a small window shows BPM, sound, the next level and a bar filling toward the next pulse.

When Android asks what to share, choose "Entire screen" — sharing a single app often does not work. Nothing from your screen leaves the phone: the picture is only compared frame to frame in memory, never stored or sent. The source code is open; you can build the app yourself.
Phone audio was stopped by Android (it ends when the phone locks). Asking to share the screen again…
Connect the Coyote and/or the Opossum first (Step 2). Close the DG-Lab app, then scan and tap CONNECT on each device.
Link A and B (same dials for both)
On: channel B mirrors every dial of channel A. Off: A and B get their own strength, waveform, intensity and pulse length, e.g. a gentle B under a stronger A, or a different pattern on each side.

Output follows how the phone is held. Tilt = how far from lying flat (0° flat, 90° upright). Movement = acceleration or rotation of the phone. Each device decides how tilt and movement drive it; the two multiply, so a factor set to "no output" silences the device.
Level zone (tilt below this counts as flat)

Gyro mode ignores music entirely. Strength comes from tilt and movement through the relations below, between each channel\'s base and max from the output dials above. Patterns loop continuously while a device is driven.
All dials, waveforms, relations, limits and the mode go back to the built-in defaults. Output stops. Connected devices stay connected. This cannot be undone.

Uses the phone\'s motion sensors while in music mode. While you keep moving (jumping, dancing), the Coyote is held off, and the hold keeps growing the longer you move. Stop for a second and the hold resets, so shocks come back. Movement sensitivity follows the "full movement" sliders in the GYRO tab.
When the limit is reached: MAX shock

On: when you have kept moving for the whole limit, a shock at MAX strength is delivered for the length below, then the hold restarts. Off: reaching the limit just lets normal shocks resume while you move.

Detects a dip: the phone accelerating downward, as when your body drops into the beat with the phone in a pocket or hand. "Votes" uses each dip as evidence for which beat is the "1", so once-per-bar shocks land on your dips. "Fires" shocks the selected devices on every dip directly, independent of the audio beat.
Drop needed to count as a dip
Chalk Cage · stay inside the box

Put the phone on a tripod facing the player, then draw a box around them on the preview and lock it. Standing, kneeling or lying all work; the app looks for a body, never a face. Step outside the box and a countdown warns you; stay out and the Coyote shocks. Nothing from the camera is stored or sent.
